Lack of US sensitivity to India’s concerns over Pakistan terrorism impacting ties: EAM Jaishankar
New York: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar says that the US’s lack of sensitivity to India’s concerns about terrorism emanating from Pakistan is a problem for Washington-New Delhi relations.
He did name Pakistan, but made it amply clear he was referring to it by ascribing the terrorism to “a neighbour” that uses it as a policy, and it was criticism directed at President Donald Trump for developing close relations with Pakistan, ignoring its role as a purveyor of terror.
Therefore, the terrorism issue is “particularly important” for India, he said.
Trump has entirely walked away from the issue of terrorism when it comes to Pakistan, in a change from the policies of the previous administrations.
Pakistan’s role as an accessory to the attacks was exposed when al-Qaida leader Osama bin Laden was found to be living under Pakistan’s protection.

India, Pakistan agree to immediate ceasefire; EAM Jaishankar reiterates country's 'uncompromising stance against terrorism'
India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri has confirmed that India and Pakistan have agreed for a ceasefire with immediate effect from 17:00 on May 10. This comes after US President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that India and Pakistan have agreed for a "full and immediate ceasefire." India's foreign minister S Jaishankar also confirmed that both countries worked together to stop "firing and military action."
India and Pakistan have today worked out an understanding on stoppage of firing and military action.India has consistently maintained a firm and uncompromising stance against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. It will continue to do so.
Trump shared a post on Truth Social saying,"After a long night of talks mediated by the United States, I am pleased to announce that India and Pakistan have agreed to a FULL AND IMMEDIATE CEASEFIRE. Congratulations to both Countries on using Common Sense and Great Intelligence. Thank you for your attention to this matter!"

“What for us in India is particularly important is the issue of terrorism. That we feel that…as a country perhaps there are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbour as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many, many decades,” Jaishankar said, making a reference to Pakistan.

passages.title: Why Balochistan observes August 11 as its 'Independence Day': The history behind the date
passages.passage:
Why Balochistan observes August 11 as its 'Independence Day': The history behind the date
In light of renewed debates and discussions about Balochistan within the politics of South Asia, there is a certain date that comes to prominence on a regular basis: August 11. Each year, numerous Baloch national movements celebrate this day as the Independence Day of Balochistan, because it denotes the brief period of time when the Khanate of Kalat existed as an independent state prior to joining Pakistan.
Recently, Baloch representative and diplomat Mir Yar Baloch took to X (formerly Twitter) and shared, "The Republic of Balochistan announces worldwide celebrations of August 11 as the Independence Day of Balochistan with national unity."
While the Baloch nationalists observe August 11 as marking the day of independence for their land, Pakistan claims the legitimacy of its accession in 1948.

passages.title: Balochistan declares August 11 as Independence Day, renews call for global recognition after breaking away from Pakistan
passages.passage:
Balochistan declares August 11 as Independence Day, renews call for global recognition after breaking away from Pakistan
Weeks after declaring independence from Pakistan, the self-proclaimed Republic of Balochistan on Monday announced that August 11 would be observed as the Independence Day of Balochistan and appealed to Baloch communities across the world to mark the occasion with nationwide celebrations, reported CNN-News18.
In a statement, the Republic of Balochistan called on the international community to recognise what it described as an independent and sovereign Balochistan, while urging people across the Baloch nation to commemorate the day with unity.
According to the statement, the Republic of Balochistan regards August 11 as its Independence Day and said the occasion would be observed every year.

passages.title: 6.4 Magnitude Earthquake Hits Central Japan, No Tsunami Warning Yet
passages.passage:
6.4 Magnitude Earthquake Hits Central Japan, No Tsunami Warning Yet
A strong earthquake of magnitude 6.4 jolted Japan’s Ishikawa and other central Japan prefectures on Tuesday, the country’s weather agency said.
According to the preliminary information, the earthquake occurred at a depth of around 10 km off the western coast of the prefecture measuring a lower 5 on the Japanese seismic scale of 7 in Ishkiwara’s Noto, a region which is still recovering from the deadly January 1 earthquakes.
The Japanese Meteorological Agency (JMA) had said that at least 155 earthquakes along with the aforementioned 7.5-magnitude earthquake (and the 6-magnitude aftershock that followed closely after) struck Japan on January 1.
The massive earthquake had toppled buildings, triggered landslides and sparked a massive fire. Video footage shared on social media and also shared by Japanese local news outlets showed restaurant doors and street signs shaking due to the intensity of the earthquake. At a karaoke bar in Ishikawa, people were heard crying for help as tables were recorded shaking intensely following the earthquake, spilling drinks from glasses.

passages.title: 5.7-magnitude earthquake hits central Japan, injuring at least 20
passages.passage:
At least 20 people were injured after a 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Japan early on Sunday, local media reported.
Kyodo News reported injuries in Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures, citing local authorities.
The earthquake originated in the western part of Shizuoka prefecture at a depth of about 40 kilometres (25 miles), according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.
The quake was the strongest to hit Aichi in about three decades.
A 4.3 magnitude earthquake hit the Kumamoto prefecture in southwestern Japan on Sunday morning.
Japan, which sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire and directly atop four major tectonic plates, is one of the most seismically active countries in the world.

passages.title: Magnitude 5.7 Earthquake Hits Central Japan, Injuring Over 20 and Delaying High-Speed Rail
passages.passage:
Magnitude 5.7 Earthquake Hits Central Japan, Injuring Over 20 and Delaying High-Speed Rail
A magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck central Japan early Sunday, injuring dozens of residents and causing widespread transit delays across key transportation corridors. The tremor occurred at 1:04 a.m.
local time on Sunday, November 8, 2026 (16:04 GMT on Saturday, November 7), according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.
Local authorities across Aichi and Shizuoka prefectures reported that at least 20 to 24 people sustained injuries during the shaking. Officials noted that the injuries primarily resulted from falls, accidents on stairs, and individuals tumbling from their beds as the ground shook in the middle of the night.
The earthquake temporarily disrupted high-speed rail operations in Japan's central economic corridor. The Tokaido Shinkansen bullet train operated at reduced speeds between Shizuoka and Gifu-Hashima while personnel conducted track and safety inspections, before returning to normal-speed service before noon on Sunday.

passages.title: At Least 20 Injured After Magnitude 5.7 Earthquake Hits Central Japan
passages.passage:
Tokyo, November 08 (QNA) - At least 20 people were injured after a magnitude 5.7 earthquake struck western Shizuoka Prefecture in central Japan early Sunday, triggering strong tremors across several prefectures, Japanese authorities said.The earthquake struck at a depth of approximately 40 kilometers, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA). It registered a maximum intensity of 5-upper on Japan's seismic intensity scale in parts of Aichi Prefecture.Strong shaking was also recorded in parts of Shizuoka, Aichi, Gifu and Nagano prefectures, while long-period ground motion of Level 1 was observed in parts of Nagano and Aichi, according to the JMA.No tsunami warning was issued following the earthquake.The quake disrupted some local train services, while other services were operated at reduced speeds as a precautionary measure.Japan is highly prone to earthquakes because it lies along the Pacific Ring of Fire. Bush’s brother crosses party lines to vote for James Talarico for Senate
Neil Bush, a son of former president George HW Bush and a lifelong Republican, announced on Tuesday that he crossed party lines to vote for James Talarico, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Texas.
In a Facebook post, Neil Bush said he chose to vote early for Talarico over Ken Paxton, the Republican candidate and current Texas attorney general, because he was “deeply troubled” by Paxton’s conduct and was “enormously impressed” by Talarico’s principles.
“I have been a Republican for most of my life, and I still believe deeply in many traditional Republican principles. But character matters more than party affiliation. Our democracy depends on leaders who respect our institutions, tell the truth, accept accountability, and seek to unite rather than divide,” Neil Bush wrote.

George W. Bush’s daughter, brother throw weight behind James Talarico
Former President George W. Bush’s daughter Barbara and his brother Neil have broken with their family’s political party in the high-stakes race to support Democratic nominee James Talarico, adding to Republican anxiety about the contest.
On Tuesday, in another Bush defection, the former president’s brother said on Facebook that he had cast his vote for Talarico in early voting.
“I have never posted a political message on Facebook not wanting to offend friends whose views may be very different than mine. I’m breaking that tradition because I voted early today, and I voted for James Talarico for the United States Senate,” Neil Bush wrote in a lengthy post. “My vote was motivated by two things: deep concern about Ken Paxton’s record and genuine admiration for the character and principles I see in James Talarico.”

United Nations: 81st General Assembly opens in New York
The atmosphere is one of “an era of profound uncertainty,” in the words of UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, as the 81st United Nations General Assembly opens its debate on Tuesday, September 22. Heads of state and government from around the world are taking part, addressing international challenges ranging from security and geopolitical tensions to economic issues and artificial intelligence.
Expectations are generally realistic, with few anticipating any major breakthroughs. There is, however, considerable attention on what will happen away from the spotlight of the General Assembly chamber—namely, the bilateral meetings focused on the ongoing conflicts. A meeting between UN Secretary-General Guterres and Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov is already scheduled for September 24.
For the first time in its history, the General Assembly has also placed artificial intelligence at the top of its agenda—seeking a global agreement to establish limits on its development and use. Guterres has included AI among the “three existential threats” of our time, alongside the climate crisis and growing inequality.

A paradox of being pope is that you live most of your life before you know what story you are really in. The genial John XXIII once berated God in jest: “He knew from all eternity that I would be pope … Don’t you think he could have made me a little more photogenic?” Leo XIV has a handsomer face than John, but he has a similar problem. He is not in control of his backstory — as recent controversies surrounding his decision to vote in the US midterm elections and now his trip to South America have begun to show.
Leo is, for many, the first American pope: the anti-Trump who embodies a gentler, more cosmopolitan set of stars and stripes. Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina from Uruguay on Sunday, beginning the country’s first papal visit in nearly four decades and the most politically sensitive stop of his Latin American tour. In his first public address, he implicitly challenged President Javier Milei’s austerity agenda, saying the economy should serve people and highlighting the needs of poor households, pensioners and people with disabilities. He also urged Milei and other leaders to safeguard democracy through listening, respectful language, respect for institutions and efforts to reach agreement. The remarks contrasted with Milei’s spending cuts and divisive rhetoric as Argentina remains deeply polarized. During the visit, Leo went to a Catholic home for about 400 people with disabilities; its coordinator said government supplies, including medication, special food and diapers, had not arrived since November, in a dispute being heard in court. The visit also carries the legacy of Pope Francis, who never returned to Argentina during his papacy.

But some of the industry’s own supporters pointed elsewhere: at President Donald Trump and the roughly $1.4 billion in income he generated from crypto ventures last year.
Now the industry is confronting the other side of its embrace of Trump: The alliance brought major wins in Washington, only for the president’s own crypto dealings to become an obstacle to locking some of those gains into law.
Then Trump’s business dealings became part of the perceived problem. Several people in the industry now say his financial ties to crypto helped turn an already difficult bill into an even harder sell.

passages.title: Crypto’s Trump-Fueled Washington Boom Reaches Its Endgame
passages.passage:
(Bloomberg) -- Crypto's extraordinary run of political good fortune in Washington has come to an abrupt halt. With Democrats set to control Congress following their midterm sweep, the industry faces the prospect of tougher rules and closer scrutiny of its ties to President Donald Trump.
Now crypto faces the harder test of becoming a lasting force in finance as its extraordinary political advantage evaporates. The Democratic sweep threatens to make comprehensive legislation harder to secure on the industry's preferred terms and raises the prospect of congressional investigations into Trump's crypto dealings.
Trump famously launched his own digital assets, welcomed crypto executives to the White House and made the industry's ambitions part of his political agenda. In turn, crypto's biggest victories became closely associated with his presidency, even as his personal financial interests complicated the industry's efforts to secure broader political support.

Nepal’s Vice President Ramsahay Prasad Yadav, Minister for Foreign Affairs Shisir Khanal, Chief Secretary Govinda Bahadur Karki, Chief of the Army Staff General Ashok Raj Sigdel, Former Chiefs of the Army Staff, Nepali Army, Secretaries of different ministries, Ambassador of India to Nepal and Defence Attaches of friendly foreign countries were also present at the investiture ceremony.

passages.title: Fact Check: Video shows India's indigenous bullet train? No, video is from Taiwan
passages.passage:
Fact Check: Video shows India's indigenous bullet train? No, video is from Taiwan
An X user, Deepa Sharma, shared the video with the caption, “The future is here... India all set to see and ride its first own bullet train.”
A reverse image search using keyframes from the viral video led us to a report published by Taiwanese news outlet TVBS on August 17, 2026, titled, ‘22 years after noting each other! The new high-speed rail train "N700ST" officially arrived in Taiwan, and the street railway fans rushed to take pictures.’
The TVBS report also included a video showing the transportation of the train. The visuals match those seen in the viral clip.
The N700ST is a new-generation high-speed train procured by Taiwan High Speed Rail from Japan. According to an official announcement by Taiwan High Speed Rail, the first set of the 12-car train arrived at Pier 74 of Kaohsiung Port on August 15, 2026.
India's first indigenous bullet train is being manufactured for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail corridor at the BEML facility in Bengaluru.

passages.title: Fact-Check: Does This Viral Video Show India’s First Bullet Trains? No!
passages.passage:
Fact-Check: Does This Viral Video Show India’s First Bullet Trains? No!
A video showing a train coach, with a saffron stripe along its body, being transported atop a heavy vehicle, has gone viral on social media.
What's the claim?: Those sharing the short clip have claimed that it shows a glimpse of India's first bullet trains, which are being indigenously manufactured at Bengaluru's BEML Limited in partnership with the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) under the Indian Railways.
But....?: The claim is false. The video shows the N700ST bullet train in Taiwan's Kaohsiung, not India.
Adding Kaohsiung to our previous search term, we came across more news reports by Japan Times and Kaohsiung Times, which also reported on the train's arrival in Taiwan.
Conclusion: A video showing a N700ST train arriving in Taiwan's Kaohsiung is being shared with the false claim that it shows India's first bullet train.

"India-Japan discussions on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail are, in fact, progressing well. Japan will provide the E20 train series, but only in the early 2030s. The train in question is under development," he said.

Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, has become a key migration route as thousands attempt to cross from Morocco and many later return.
Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in North Africa, has become a major migration route from Morocco into EU territory.
For thousands of migrants who crossed from Morocco into Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta, reaching European territory did not mean the journey continued as many had expected. Many arrived hoping to move further into Europe, but within days a large number returned to Morocco after finding themselves unable to travel onwards and facing uncertainty about what would happen next.
Ceuta’s importance goes beyond its size. The enclave shows how geography has placed a small Spanish territory at the centre of a wider debate over migration, border security and relations between Europe and North Africa. For many migrants, the journey ended almost where it began — at the Morocco border — but the pressures pushing people towards Ceuta continue to shape one of Europe’s most closely watched migration routes.

passages.passage:
India’s poverty rate has fallen, but challenges remain: Jobs, AI, ageing population
The World Bank also estimates that the poverty rate, as per $4.2-per-day threshold, fell further to 14.2% in 2026 and may fall to 12.1% by 2028. These figures will be updated as labour market and macroeconomic data are revised or new numbers become available.
But the projected decline in the poverty rate — by 2028 and beyond — hinges on a key development: India’s poorest states creating productive jobs. The World Bank noted that youth unemployment has increased over the past year to 15.9%, and real earnings have not moved much.
Luckily, a Reserve Bank of India (RBI) staff paper last year updated India’s last official poverty line, set by a committee led by former central bank governor C Rangarajan.
The Rangarajan poverty line had caused a stir in 2014 when it estimated the national poverty line at Rs 1,407 in terms of monthly per capita expenditure for urban areas and Rs 972 for rural areas. What this meant was that anyone spending more than Rs 47 per day in urban areas or Rs 32 per day in rural areas was not poor. This led to India’s poverty rate being pegged at 29.5%.

passages.title: Argentina poverty rises to 32 percent under Milei with more pain forecast | Inequality News
passages.passage:
Argentina’s poverty rate has risen, hitting 32.3 percent in the first half of 2026 under President Javier Milei, partly erasing the country’s earlier gains.
According to figures released by the national statistics agency INDEC on Thursday, the poverty rate rose 4.1 percentage points between January and June compared with the last half of 2025, moving from 28.2 to 32.3 percent.
Extreme poverty — where households cannot afford basic food needs — also rose from 6.3 to 7.5 percent.
Estimates from the Catholic University of Argentina (UCA), widely seen as an early indicator of official poverty trends, suggest the poverty rate could rise to 35 percent by the end of the year.
Poverty surged to nearly 53 percent in the first half of 2024 after his government’s devaluation of the peso and sweeping spending cuts sharply reduced purchasing power. But the rate then fell rapidly as Milei’s austerity drive eased inflation, reaching 28.2 percent in the second half of 2025, the lowest level since early 2018.
Even with this year’s rise, the poverty rate remains below the level reached in the first half of 2024, Milei’s first year in office, when it exceeded 50 percent.

President Donald Trump is highlighting newly released economic data showing that the official U.S. poverty rate has fallen to its lowest level on record.
According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the official poverty rate fell to 10.2% in 2025, the lowest level since the government began tracking the measure in 1959.
The decline marked the second consecutive year that the official poverty rate decreased.
However, a record-low poverty rate does not mean poverty has disappeared. Approximately 34.5 million Americans were still living below the official poverty line in 2025.
The official poverty rate is also only one measure of Americans’ economic circumstances. Families can still experience financial pressure from housing, food, health care, transportation and other expenses even when their income places them above the federal poverty threshold.

Mumbai, The father of IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode, who allegedly died by suicide 10 days ago, began a sit-in protest at Azad Maidan in south Mumbai on Monday, demanding action against those responsible for his son's death.
Sahil Wakode , a second-year student, was found hanging in his hostel room on the evening of September 18, hours after he was allegedly caught using his mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination.
The IIT Bombay board earlier constituted a 10-member committee to inquire into the circumstances surrounding Sahil's death.
IIT Bombay students held a candlelight march on Friday night, demanding reconstitution of the inquiry committee. They alleged that some members of the existing panel had expressed support for Doolla.
Students' unions from other premier institutes have also extended support to the Wakode family and demanded a transparent investigation and action against those responsible for Sahil's death.

Wakode’s death has prompted protests and demands for a fair investigation. His family has alleged harassment and caste discrimination by members of the institute. Those allegations remain under investigation.

Turning Point USA announced on September 18 that Erika Kirk, the widow of its co-founder Charlie Kirk, has been unanimously elected as the organisation’s new Chief Executive Officer and chair of the board. Indian Army debunks claims of Chinese troops advancing 50 km into Arunachal Pradesh
The Indian Army has debunked social media claims that Chinese forces defeated Indian troops and advanced nearly 50 km into Arunachal Pradesh, bringing parts of Indian territory under the control of the People's Liberation Army (PLA).
The posts included claims of a 50-km Chinese advance into Arunachal Pradesh, along with videos showing soldiers in a wooded, rocky landscape. The Army described the allegations of PLA control over Indian territory as unsubstantiated.
The latest fact-check follows several other instances of misleading content about India-China face-offs in Arunachal Pradesh.
The Army has previously flagged footage of a counter-terrorism mock drill in Karnataka, a Kazakhstan special forces exercise and videos of protests against the proposed Siang dam project. These were circulated with misleading captions suggesting Chinese advances or Indian military setbacks.
The Army also exposed a digitally altered video that falsely attributed claims about Chinese control of parts of Arunachal Pradesh to Lt Gen Girish Kalia.

The Indian Army on Saturday debunked claims that Chinese forces had advanced nearly 50 km into Arunachal Pradesh and captured Indian territory, identifying them as part of a coordinated disinformation campaign allegedly carried out by six Pakistan-sponsored X accounts.
The accounts circulated false claims about alleged developments on November 6 and 7, claiming that the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) had routed Indian troops, inflicted a major military defeat and captured territory inside Arunachal Pradesh.
The posts also used videos of soldiers moving through forested terrain, falsely presenting them as footage of recent developments along the India-China border. The visuals were misrepresented to lend credibility to the fabricated claims of Chinese military advances. passages.title: Rijiju Attacks Congress After Army Debunks Videos Of Chinese Incursions
passages.passage:
Rijiju Attacks Congress After Army Debunks Videos Of Chinese Incursions
New Delhi: Union minister Kiren Rijiju, on Tuesday, demanded an apology from the Congress after the Indian Army debunked two videos shared by a party spokesperson that falsely claimed incursions into Indian territory and control over parts of Arunachal Pradesh by the Chinese.

Half of middle-aged women live with chronic pain. Here's what we know
Chronic pain disproportionately affects women. (Getty Images: NickyLloyd)
Women are up to 70 per cent more likely to experience chronic pain than men, according to a recent report from the International Menopause Society (IMS).
In women, these pain symptoms often appear in midlife, likely due to factors such as fluctuating hormones, menopause-related biological shifts, lack of sleep and lifestyle changes.
The IMS report estimates about half of all middle-aged women experience chronic pain, describing the condition as "often under-recognised, under-diagnosed and inadequately treated".
"Chronic pain in midlife is a very important subject and highly neglected," she says.

passages.title: It's Not In Your Head: New Study Proves Why Women Feel Chronic Pain Differently
passages.passage: Chronic pain is a complex health condition wherein persistent pain is experienced for months, even years, without a definite cause. According to the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and affiliated bodies like the National Centre for Disease Informatics and Research (NCDIR), chronic pain is emerging as a major public health issue in India due to the startling figures. The figures indicate a steep rise, as about 19 to 25% of Indian adults report chronic pain lasting more than 3 months. Out of this figure, women are disproportionately affected, with the recorded rates nearly 1.5 times higher than men, especially pain in the bones, muscles, joints, tendons, and ligaments, and due to nervous system dysfunction.

Covid-19 lockdowns caused more chronic pain in women than men. Here's why
A new study has found that the pandemic lockdown caused an increase in chronic pain, especially in women.
"With chronic pain affecting around 20 per cent of the EU adult population, it is vital to understand how people living with chronic pain are being affected by the pandemic and to develop pain management interventions that clearly target women," Lang-Illievich added.
Responses indicated that women with chronic pain perceived increased pain severity during the first lockdown, compared to their typical pain levels prior to lockdown. While average pain intensity scored (VAS 0-100) before the first COVID-19 lockdown was similar in men (46.5) and women (45), the average change in pain intensity was much lower in men (0.8) than women (3.9).
"Although reported pain intensity between men and women was similar before COVID-19, our data clearly show that women experienced a higher aggravation of chronic pain during the first lockdown," said Lang-Illievich.

At least six people were killed and 15 others injured after a gunman opened fire on pedestrians from a moving car in Krakow's Main Market Square in southern Poland on Saturday, November 7. The 25-year-old suspect, a Polish national, was shot and wounded by police before being arrested and taken to hospital. The Krakow Carriage Driver's Association told PAP that several horse-drawn carriage drivers were seriously injured in the shooting.

passages.title: Trump Losses May Not Slow Europe’s Far-Right Advance
passages.passage:
The Republican Party’s midterm rout has energized European opponents of right-wing populism, who see it as a possible setback for political movements backed by President Donald Trump. But the result does not guarantee a similar reversal in Europe: far-right parties remain strong in countries including France, where Marine Le Pen leads polls, and Spain, where the campaign is taking shape ahead of a November election. Spain’s acting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has urged voters to deliver a broad victory against the far right, while analysts say defeats for populists elsewhere could either weaken their momentum or leave anti-establishment challengers positioned to benefit from anger at incumbents. The outcome may also affect transatlantic ties and calculations on security, though Trump retains substantial foreign-policy powers and Europe remains reliant on NATO.

Home Office was housing 16,021 asylum seekers across 160 hotels at end of June, while small boat crossings down 23%
The number of asylum seekers living in hotels has halved in a year, Home Office figures show.
Sweeping changes to the asylum system have also led to a significant drop in legal arrivals and asylum claims, but the numbers of asylum seekers housed in private accommodation has increased as the government moves people from hotels into privately rented houses in multiple occupation (HMOs).

The Guardian revealed this month that the government was considering paying higher prices for housing asylum seekers in private rental properties as part of Andy Burnham’s plan to spread accommodation more evenly across the country.

passages.title: Will one-stop blood tests for cancer save lives?
passages.passage:
Will one-stop blood tests for cancer save lives?
The principle behind cancer-spotting blood tests is relatively simple. Some, like Galleri, analyse DNA fragments shed by cancer cells, whereas others look for proteins or metabolites that those cells produce. Cancerguard, a rival test developed by Exact Sciences, an American company, combines multiple approaches.
Scientific advances reported by several academic groups in the past three years, however, may soon lead to more sophisticated and powerful tests, says Dr Schuh. In addition to using less destructive ways to identify methylation, some new methods scan the entire genome for cancerous changes in the DNA code. New tests also analyse patterns in the physical features of DNA fragments that may hold clues about the presence of cancer. Such multi-pronged approaches, supported by artificial intelligence tools to assist with data analysis, hold promise. If they can be turned into reliable tests, they may well help identify which cancers need prompt action and which do not.

The NHS is launching a trial for a new blood test capable of detecting multiple different cancers.
Patients aged over 45 with these symptoms will be recruited at 200 GP surgeries and offered the test which looks for DNA shed by tumours as well as tell tale proteins in the blood.
Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said: "The earlier cancers are diagnosed, the more chance they can be successfully treated, and lives can be saved. This world-first trial will establish whether simple blood tests can help GPs identify much sooner the patients who need urgent support.”
The new blood tests aim to detect early markers of cancer before severe symptoms develop to catch and treat them before they progress. Professor Peter Johnson, NHS England’s director for cancer, said: “Detecting abdomen cancer early is notoriously difficult because the symptoms can easily be mistaken for other less serious conditions but the NHS is determined to find a solution.

passages.title: 'Election Day Is Wednesday': FBI Gives Voters Wrong Date While Promising to Protect Midterms, Slammed for Misinformation
passages.passage:
Hours before polls opened for the US midterm elections, the FBI's New Haven field office told voters the wrong date for Election Day in a post promoting the bureau's work to protect the vote.
'Election day is Wednesday and the #FBI is working around the clock to ensure the midterms are safe,' the account wrote on X at about 4:00 p.m. ET on Monday, 2 November, roughly 14 hours before Connecticut's polling places opened.
Election Day is Tuesday, 3 November. Federal law fixes the general election on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, and Connecticut polls are open from 6:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., according to the office of Governor Ned Lamont.
By late Monday, X users had attached a Community Note stating that Election Day falls on Tuesday, 3 November. Its second line read: 'Not Wednesday'.
New Haven, home to the FBI field office, is the only Connecticut municipality the Justice Department plans to monitor on Election Day, according to the Connecticut Secretary of the State's office. Two teams of two will check sites covered by federal Spanish-language assistance rules, state officials said.

passages.title: Kash Patel Caught In the Middle After FBI’s Embarrassing Election Day Typo Sets Off a Firestorm Among Voters
passages.passage:
Kash Patel, President Donald Trump’s handpicked selection to run the Federal Bureau of Investigation, has become one of the most lambasted officials in the federal government.
Most voters likely know they must cast a vote in the midterms by Tuesday, Nov. 3. It seems one FBI branch failed to recognize a blatant error about the highly contested election.
According to reports, the FBI’s New Haven office publicized the wrong Election Day information. The post reportedly stayed online for hours before being taken down.
“Election Day is Wednesday and the #FBI is working around the clock to ensure the midterms are safe,” read the now-deleted tweet.
“Why is the FBI falsely telling people that the election is on Wednesday?” journalist Ken Klippenstein wondered in his own Nov. 2-dated tweet.
Another asked, “Are we supposed to believe that Kash Patel’s FBI is so incompetent they can’t even figure out what day the election is on?”

US Midterms: In Maine, Democrat Troy Jackson defeats five-term Republican Senator Susan Collins
Democrat Troy Jackson defeated five-term Republican Susan Collins in Maine, giving the party their seventh flipped seat and expanding their new majority.
“I called Troy Jackson tonight to congratulate him and to assure him that my staff and I will work to ensure a smooth transition,” Collins said in a statement. “It has been the honor of my life to serve the people of Maine in the United States Senate.”
Collins had turned back challengers for nearly 30 years by emphasizing her moderate positions and ability to bring federal money to Maine. She won reelection in 2020 even as Trump lost the state by nine percentage points, serving as the only Republican in New England’s congressional delegation. No Republican presidential candidate has carried Maine in almost four decades.
A long-time champion of organized labor from rural northern Maine, Jackson ran as a progressive, calling for higher taxes on the wealthy and for US Immigration and Customs Enforcement to be abolished.

passages.title: Democrat Troy Jackson defeats Susan Collins to win Maine US Senate seat in blow to Republicans
passages.passage:
Democrat Troy Jackson defeats Susan Collins to win Maine US Senate seat in blow to Republicans
The Democrat Troy Jackson has won Maine’s US Senate race, toppling five-term Republican incumbent Susan Collins in one of the biggest upsets of the 2026 midterms.
A lumberjack by trade and former state senate president, Jackson sought to break down Collins’s carefully crafted image as a moderate Republican willing to break with the Donald Trump, painting her instead as a loyal supporter of the president.
“We did it. Working people won,” Jackson declared at a victory party in Maine before a crowd of his supporters. “And I’m feeling damn proud to be standing here with you all tonight – or this morning, I guess now.”
Collins, meanwhile, cast Jackson as ideologically inconsistent and lacking the experience needed to deliver for Maine at the federal level.
Maine Democrats had just weeks to organize a special convention to select a replacement for Platner. After Jackson won, he had just 101 days to mount a Senate campaign.

passages.title: Troy Jackson wins Maine Senate race over Susan Collins, in big victory for Democrats
passages.passage:
Troy Jackson wins Maine Senate race over Susan Collins, in big victory for Democrats
Troy Jackson speaks at the Bangor Cross Insurance Center on July 24, 2026 in Bangor, Maine. Ashley L. Conti for NPR hide caption
Troy Jackson has defeated Republican incumbent Susan Collins for U.S. Senate in Maine, according to a race call by the Associated Press, a crucial victory for Democrats in their push to win back the Senate majority.
The Democratic Party has long tried to oust Collins, and at a moment when President Trump's approval ratings are at historic lows, Democrats saw Maine as one of their best opportunities to flip a Republican seat.
As the longest-serving Republican woman in the Senate, Collins entered the race with a history of defying national political headwinds, repeatedly winning in a state that has consistently voted for Democrats at the state level. But that streak ended Tuesday night.
The results bring Collins' nearly 30-year tenure in Congress to a close and make Jackson the first Democrat to represent Maine in the Senate since 1995.

This time the headwinds were stronger. They included Trump’s unpopular war with Iran and its effect on fuel prices, and a polarising agenda that the Republican-led Congress had largely left unchecked. The president said they would speak again after he returned to the White House, but his remarks suggested he was not keen on retaining her as the administration’s chief spokesperson.
A White House official told CNN that Zacharia was “transitioning out” of the role, while a Trump adviser said she would leave the White House within the next few days.
Trump, who praised Zacharia as a loyal supporter and said she had been mistreated by the media, nevertheless appeared to question whether she was suited to the position.

Not only Sonam Wangchuk, AISA activists on parallel hunger strike ‘at high risk’ too: ‘Shows the govt is heartless’
There's the hunger that gnaws at the stomach, and then “the hunger for power that people in government have” — that was the contrast Neha Bora offered this week for the fast she and two other student activists have kept up for 20 days and counting at Jantar Mantar, parallel to activist Sonam Wangchuk's fast under the banner of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).
Doctors have warned their bodies are beginning to fail them, and at least three other comrades from the CPI(ML)-Liberation-affiliated AISA have had to be taken to hospital already. According to the organisation, Aameen is “at risk of hypovolemic shock” due to dehydration; Neha's blood sugar level has dropped to a dangerous 49 mg/dL; and Manish has lost more than 10 per cent of his body weight.

Activist Sonam Wangchuk said on Friday that he won't be participating in the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)'s Jantar Mantar protest on October 10, saying that he is busy making preparations for the upcoming winter.
The CJP is holding a protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10 as part of its nationwide campaign demanding CEC Gyanesh Kuamr's resignation over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) irregularities.
Wangchuk was one of the key figures of CJP's July protest when the youth-led movement took to streets demanding the then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over examination irregularities. The activist sat on a a hunger strike for 26 days at Jantar Mantar in support of the protesting students and ended the indefinite strike on July 23 at a hospital in Gurugram in the presence of union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, saying that he broke the fast after a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country.

Ottawa: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Sunday extended Diwali greetings to people celebrating the festival in Canada and around the world, describing it as a symbol of the triumph of light over darkness, good over evil and knowledge over ignorance.
In a message on the occasion, Carney said communities across Canada were joining millions of people worldwide to celebrate the Festival of Lights, with families and friends gathering to light diyas, share meals and honour traditions passed down through generations.

Carney spoke after Democrats won a sweeping midterm victory in the United States. The result set up new pressure in Congress to challenge Trumps trade measures. Carney said Canada still wanted an agreement that suited Canadian interests. Carney did not say if the election changed Canada’s bargaining stance with Washington.
Canada paused trade talks in August after US demands raised concerns in Ottawa. Carney said those demands threatened Canadian sovereignty and French-language protections. passages.passage:
Gandak surge eases; Bihar embankments withstand after Nepal upstream floods
The surge in the Gandak River waters triggered by upstream flash floods in Nepal and Tibet receded overnight, even as over 4,000 people were evacuated from parts of Bihar around midnight on Thursday. Officials allayed fears, saying embankments withstood the pressure and water levels were returning to normal.
The Valmiki Nagar barrage in West Champaran recorded its highest discharge of around 1.50 lakh cusec around midnight. By early morning, the flow had stabilised. At about 7am, the discharge was at 95,200 cusec. It receded to around 88,000 cusec by 8 am, said Bihar water resources department secretary Chandra Shekhar Singh.
Authorities sounded a high alert across Bihar’s north-western districts following floods in the Bhote Koshi into Nepal’s Trishuli-Narayani system, which feeds the Gandak.
Floods washed away roads, bridges, houses, and power projects, killing 160 people and leaving at least 750 others unaccounted for after ice, mud, and rocks collapsed into a Himalayan river at the Nepal-China border near Tibet on Wednesday morning.

Amid massive floods, Bihar's Gandak river swells after Nepal rain fury
Fed by heavy rains in Nepal, the Gandak river swelled to a record level on Tuesday, damaging embankments in the West Champarandistrict and threatening widespread inundation in Bihar already bruised by a massive flood.
The Water Resources Department said the water level in the Gandak river hit a record 91.25 metres at Bagaha following heavy rain in Nepal. This was 0.35 metres higher than what was recorded in 2024.
Two stretches of the Champaran embankment at Khairatwa in Bagaha-1 and Phuliyakhad in Bairia on the left bank of the Gandak were damaged overnight due to excessive water discharge from the Valmikinagar barrage following intense rainfall in Nepal, it said.

"At the Gandak Barrage in Valmikinagar, the discharge stood at 1,86,200 cusecs at 10 am, down from 1,91,200 cusecs at 8 am on Monday. At Kosi Barrage in Birpur, it was 1,20,055 cusecs at 10 am and 1,51,116 cusecs at the Sone Barrage in Indrapuri, the department said.

passages.title: Nepal flash floods: Bihar on high alert as floodwaters reach Gandak Barrage, all 36 gates opened
passages.passage:
Nepal flash floods: Bihar on high alert as floodwaters reach Gandak Barrage, all 36 gates opened
Bihar was put on high alert on Wednesday as floodwaters from Nepal entered the Gandak river and reached the Gandak Barrage, prompting authorities to open all 36 gates to control the surge, officials said.
The barrage is situated at Valmikinagar in West Champaran, the northernmost district of the state that shares a border with Nepal.
Nearly 100 people were killed and over 750, including 133 Indian nationals, remain missing after a massive flash flood originating in Tibet swept through central Nepal, devastating several towns and villages, washing away critical bridges, and crippling a dozen hydropower projects.
Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the parliament that an earthquake hit the Tibet region at 8:37 am (local time) and the flash floods were reported three minutes later, suggesting the tremors may have caused a glacial outburst which triggered the floods.
Opening of 36 gates of the Gandak Barrage can facilitate the flow of the water and help control the flood situation, officials of the department said.

Bihar was put on high alert on Wednesday as floodwaters from Nepal entered the Gandak river and reached the barrage, prompting the authorities concerned to open all 36 gates to control the surge.
"The water discharge from the Gandak barrage at Valmikinagar peaked at 1.50 lakh cusecs at 11 pm on Wednesday, after which the water level began receding," the Water Resources Department said in a statement on Thursday.
The Nepal Police said that the death toll rose to 162 in the flash flood on the Bhotekoshi River that wreaked havoc across three districts on Wednesday.

passages.title: Washington state passes ballot measure banning trans girls from school sports
passages.passage:
Washington state passes ballot measure banning trans girls from school sports
Voters in Washington state have passed a ballot measure banning transgender girls from playing on girls’ sports teams, a major loss for LGBTQ+ rights in a solidly Democratic state.
Critics of the sports bans argue they subject all girls to harmful scrutiny of their bodies, with opponents of Initiative 638 warning it could “force tens of thousands of Washington girls each year to undergo invasive, embarrassing, and potentially harmful genital exams just to play sports”.
The initiative was introduced in 2025 by a political action committee called Let’s Go Washington, which was founded by Brian Heywood, a hedge fund manager who has funded conservative measures. The measure was considered the most restrictive of the four trans youth sports bans on state ballots this year, as it mandates that girls prove their sex through hormone or genetic tests, or genital examinations. The measure only applies to women’s sports, and boys are not required to undergo any similar procedures.

passages.title: Washington 2026 ballot measures
passages.passage:
As of November 8, 2026, three statewide ballot measures have been certified to appear on the Washington ballot on November 3, 2026.
Citizens of Washington may initiate legislation as either a direct state statute— called Initiative to the People (ITP) in Washington— or indirect state statute— called Initiative to the Legislature (ITL) in Washington. In Washington, citizens also have the power to repeal legislation via veto referendum. Citizens may not initiate constitutional amendments. The Washington State Legislature, however, may place legislatively referred constitutional amendments on the ballot with a two-thirds (66.67%) vote in each chamber. The Washington Legislature may refer measures to the 2026 ballot during the 2025 and 2026 state legislative sessions.
In Washington, a total of 510 ballot measures appeared on statewide ballots between 1889 and 2024. A total of 268 ballot measures were approved, and 242 ballot measures were defeated.

After cancer surgery, Pope Leo embarks on Latin America trip
ROME — Pope Leo XIV is kicking off a three-nation tour of Latin America with a visit to Uruguay, the region's least Catholic and most secular country, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery that had put the entire trip into question.
Leo will find in Uruguay a country unlike any other in Latin America, which is home to around 40% of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics. Uruguay is considered the most secular country in the region, where only a fraction of people who identify as Catholic actually go to Mass regularly.
Uruguay was the first country in the world to legalize marijuana for recreational use, the second country in Latin America to decriminalize abortion, and the third country in the Americas to legalize same-sex marriage.
"It seems that the pope's presence is shifting something here and is gradually breaking down this veil that has always sought to obscure and diminish the presence of the Catholic tradition that lies at the country's foundation," said Guzmán Carriquiry, the Uruguayan former head of the Vatican's pontifical commission for Latin America.

The United States has reported more than 5,000 measles cases in 2026, marking the highest number in 35 years, according to official figures released on Friday. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the country's leading public health agency, reported 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but largely preventable disease across the country so far this year. passages.title: CDC Confirms US Measles Cases Hit 35-Year High
passages.passage:
CDC Confirms US Measles Cases Hit 35-Year High
Washington, United States: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday.
So far in 2026, 5,182 confirmed cases of the highly contagious but highly preventable disease have been reported across the country, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the nation's leading public health agency.
That compares with 2,289 cases during all of 2025, and is the highest level recorded by the CDC since 1991.
State health officials have reported at least eight measles-related deaths, including among very young children.
Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms and a rash, and in some cases more serious complications such as pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to severe long-term health problems or even death.

The United States has recorded 5,182 confirmed cases of measles since the beginning of 2026, according to the report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) published on Friday, November 6. This count, as of November 5, is the highest since 1991.
Children under five represent 18% of the cases, while those aged 5 to 19 account for 41%. Together, children and adolescents thus make up 59% of the confirmed infections.
The national total already exceeds double the 2,289 cases recorded for the entire year 2025. The CDC counts 43 new outbreaks in 2026 and attributes 4,993 cases, or 96% of the total, to epidemic clusters, some of which began in 2025.
The CDC emphasizes that national averages can mask local pockets of low vaccination, where the virus can spread rapidly. The agency reminds that two doses of the MMR vaccine provide 97% protection against measles. The case numbers for 2025 and 2026 remain provisional.

(Bloomberg) -- A Houthi attack damaged one of the landmarks of the Saudi Arabian capital’s financial district, upsetting plans for a return to normal about a month after deadly strikes on Riyadh’s airport disrupted travel and canceled showpiece events.
The Iranian-backed Houthis in Yemen, who’ve been fighting Saudi Arabia for a decade, claimed responsibility. Saudi authorities later said they’d retaliated by destroying two missile launchers used in attempted attacks.
The rare strike on Riyadh’s financial hub, known as KAFD, will do little to reassure international companies already buffeted by months of regional conflict. KAFD hosts Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund as well as the stock exchange, global consultancies and finance heavyweights including Goldman Sachs and Brookfield.
The latest attacks risk spurring more travel restrictions for executives who shuttle back and forth to Riyadh from hubs such as Dubai, Abu Dhabi and London. They came almost a month after Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s main airport killed more than a dozen people and injured hundreds more.

Two ballistic missiles and two cruise missiles were intercepted by the air defences that were targeting Riyadh and other regions, the Saudi Arabia-led coalition said. It accused Houthi rebels of launching the ballistic missiles, who haven’t claimed responsibility as yet.
The strikes in Saudi Arabia come after Riyadh carried out airstrikes in Yemen’s capital, Sanaa, on Saturday, which is controlled by the Houthis. Officials from the rebel group had said that strikes killed at least 27 people.

The Japanese government lowered its travel advisory level for Israel on Thursday, according to the Israeli Foreign Ministry, itself citing an announcement by Japan's Foreign Ministry.
The decision followed ongoing dialogue between Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, the statement noted.
The Foreign Ministry emphasized the importance of the decision in terms of bilateral relations between the two countries, opening the door to more business and cooperation.
According to Japanese media reports, Israel is now considered a "Level 2" destination, meaning the Japanese government advises against unnecessary travel, down from the previous "Level 3" designation, which called for refraining from travel entirely.
The decision came alongside similar changes for other Middle Eastern countries, such as Iraq and Lebanon, which had some of their areas downgraded to Level 3 from "Level 4," which, according to Japanese media, calls for evacuation, with the entirety of Iran remaining at Level 4.

Israel's president has chosen Gadi Eisenkot, Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, to try to form a new government.
Mr Eisenkot will have 28 days to form a coalition after he receives the formal offer from the president later today.
Israel's President Isaac Herzog has announced he will give Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival, Gadi Eisenkot the first opportunity to form a new coalition government.
The decision comes days after the president met with representatives from each of the parties that had secured seats in the next Israeli parliament, the Knesset, asking them for their recommendations for who should be given the task of trying to form a new coalition.
"During the round of consultations, factions totalling 67 members of Knesset recommended to President Herzog that Yashar Leader Gadi Eisenkot be tasked with forming the government," a statement from Mr Herzog's office read.

passages.title: Israeli President Picks Netanyahu Rival Eisenkot To Form New Government

Israeli President Picks Netanyahu Rival Eisenkot To Form New Government
JERUSALEM (Worthy News) – Israeli President Isaac Herzog has selected opposition leader and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government, dealing a major political blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Eisenkot received the backing of 67 of Israel’s 120 lawmakers, compared with 46 supporting Netanyahu. However, forming a governing coalition could prove difficult because Eisenkot has ruled out joining forces with Arab-led parties whose support helped secure his nomination.
Netanyahu called for a national unity government bringing together Israel’s main political factions, while warning against relying on Arab-led parties that he accused of supporting terrorism.
President Herzog acknowledged that Eisenkot faced a difficult task despite receiving the most parliamentary endorsements. “The authority vested in me by law is to determine who has the ability to form a government,” he said.
If Eisenkot fails to form a government, Herzog could turn to another lawmaker, potentially Netanyahu. Another election remains possible if coalition negotiations collapse.

Israeli President picks opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot to form government in setback for Netanyahu
Israel's president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's strongest rival, to try to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power.
Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he would have a majority of seats in parliament. But Arab leaders, incensed by what they view as the racist policies of Netanyahu and his far-right allies, still nominated Eisenkot to try to form a government first — giving him the most endorsements.
"President Herzog has invited Gadi Eisenkot to the President’s Residence, where he will be tasked with forming the government tomorrow," said the spokesperson of President Isaac Herzog, whose largely ceremonial role involves nominating a candidate to form a coalition after elections.

Israeli President To Invite Netanyahu's Rival, Eisenkot, To Form Govt Today | Top Points
Days after the high-stakes Knesset elections, Israeli President Isaac Herzog will formally invite Yashar Party leader Gadi Eisenkot, a rival of outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, to form the next government on Sunday.
Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, has called for a national unity government after his coalition failed to retain its parliamentary majority in the October 27 elections, despite emerging as the largest bloc.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog will formally invite Yashar Party leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government.
If Eisenkot fails to form a government, another candidate could be given the opportunity. If subsequent attempts also fail, then Israel may be forced to hold fresh elections, extending a period of political uncertainty.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog will formally invite Yashar Party leader and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government after he secured the backing of 67 lawmakers in the 120-member Knesset.

passages.title: Israel President Herzog taps Gadi Eisenkot to form government in setback for Netanyahu
passages.passage:
Israel President Herzog taps Gadi Eisenkot to form government in setback for Netanyahu
Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government after he secured 67 lawmakers’ recommendations. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to assemble a coalition and replace Benjamin Netanyahu.
Jerusalem: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has tasked opposition leader and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming the country’s next government, dealing a significant setback to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s efforts to retain power following the October 27 general election.
Eisenkot will have 28 days to form a coalition, with a possible 14-day extension if required. The development gives him the first opportunity to replace Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister.
If Eisenkot fails to form a government within 28 days, Herzog can grant him an additional 14 days. If the attempt fails, another candidate could receive the mandate, potentially giving Netanyahu another opportunity. Continued failure to form a coalition could eventually lead to fresh elections.

passages.passage:
Interviews conclude for first full-time CEO of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust
The Search Committee, for the selection of the first full-time Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra, has completed the interview process on Wednesday.
The final rounds of interviews were conducted at the Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra campus on August 11, 12. The evaluation process comprised multiple rounds designed to identify the most suitable candidates.
How 16 candidates were chosen for the final round?
Following prior online assessments, 16 candidates were selected for face-to-face interaction in Ayodhya, representing the top candidates from Defence, Bureaucracy, Corporate and Industrial sectors, Education, and Information Technology.
The evaluation focused on management skills, personality, vision, strategic plans, technology expertise and leadership potential.

passages.title: 'Ayodhya temple trust will have 15 trustees': Amit Shah on constitution of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust
passages.passage:
'Ayodhya temple trust will have 15 trustees': Amit Shah on constitution of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust
After the Uttar Pradesh cabinet on Wednesday cleared five acres of land to Sunni Central Waqf board for the construction of a mosque in Ayodhya, Home Minister Amit Shah said that the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust will have 15 trustees. Of which, one will be from the Dalit community.
"There will be 15 trustees in Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust out of which one trustee will be from Dalit society. For such an unprecedented decision that strengthens social harmony, I congratualte Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji," he tweeted.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday announced the formation of the Ram Temple trust, which would oversee the construction of Ram Temple in Ayodhya. He said that the trust has been named 'Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teertha Kshetra'.

passages.title: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust Shortlists 20 Candidates For CEO Post After Receiving 5,200 Applications
passages.passage:
Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust Shortlists 20 Candidates For CEO Post After Receiving 5,200 Applications
Uttar Pradesh: Around 20 candidates have been shortlisted for the final interview round for the post of Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust after it received around 5,200 applications.
The decision to appoint a CEO came in the wake of the alleged embezzlement of the Shri Ram temple donation fund reported in June this year. At its July 6 board meeting, the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Nyas, or temple trust, decided to appoint a chief executive officer to manage the temple affairs, TNIE reports.
Once the interviews are completed, the selection committee will shortlist three candidates and submit their names to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust for consideration. The Trust is scheduled to announce its choice for the CEO post on September 2.

BJP blasts Neha Bora over rapes in temple remark, Congress allies unsparing too
The BJP launched a sharp attack on All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora over her remarks where she said priests commit rapes inside temples. Bora came to the limelight after the NEET-UG protests and has been given a place of prominence in Opposition events by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. While the BJP used the clip to highlight what it alleged to be an "anti-Hindu mindset", some Congress allies also slammed Bora over her generalised remarks.
On October 15, the BJP had slammed Neha Bora after she called for a regime change in India, and said she drew inspiration to protest from Bangladesh's student-led demonstrations, which led to PM Sheikh Hasina's ouster in August 2024.

passages.title: Amazon brings back ‘no class-action’ clause: Why customers may have to fight disputes outside court
passages.passage:
Amazon brings back ‘no class-action’ clause: Why customers may have to fight disputes outside court
Amazon.com Inc. reintroduced a clause in its user agreement that could stop customers from filing class-action lawsuits against the company. The move gives Amazon greater legal protection against plaintiffs' attorneys, a provision it had removed five years ago.
Amazon removed a similar clause from its user agreement in 2021 amid a barrage of legal privacy challenges related to its voice-activated Alexa devices. It said customers should pursue legal claims in court in Washington state, where Amazon is based.
The company has also battled class-action lawsuits over claims of unsafe products and for allegedly making it hard to cancel Prime memberships.
The user-agreement update isn't necessarily binding in court. Plaintiffs attorneys could still seek class-action lawsuits against Amazon, and it would be up to a judge to determine if the user agreement prevents them from doing so.

The latest changes will expand the group of customers eligible for payments and raise the maximum amount some consumers can receive.
Amazon Prime customers could receive additional settlement payments as the FTC expands eligibility and raises the maximum refund to $200.

The biggest news by far is that the Amazon class is finally heading to Diablo 4 in the first half of 2027. Following the exploration of the Nahantu and Scosglen regions in Lord of Hatred, the team is bringing back the fan-favorite warrior archetype to her proper homeland of Skovos. The Amazon promises to inject a whole new combat style and tactical depth into the current roster when she arrives.
When Lord of Hatred launched earlier this year with Paladin, many fans thought the Amazon would be the second mystery class given the setting of the expansion and the class link to Skovos, but we got the Warlock at the time.
It's interesting that Diablo 4 devs seem to be striking a balance with their class rollouts, doing something completely new to the franchise (like Spiritborn and Warlock), but also bringing back some classic archetypes, starting with Paladin and now getting the Amazon from Diablo 2.

passages.title: Fact Check: Canadian Park DENIES Image Shows Niagara Falls Turning Blue Because Of Nov. 3, 2026, Blue Wave In U.S.
passages.passage:
Does a viral image show Niagara Falls lit up blue to celebrate Democrats winning control of Congress in the 2026 midterms? No, that's not true: According to the spokesperson for the body managing the falls on the Canadian side, political messaging is not allowed under the park's policies. On Nov. 3, 2026, the lights were announced as teal -- for Alzheimer's Awareness Month.
On Nov. 3, 2026, the U.S. held midterm elections, which resulted in the Democratic Party -- whose color is blue -- winning the majority in both chambers of Congress (archived here).
However, the viral image of Niagara Falls shared on social media was unrelated to that outcome.
On the Canadian side, the falls are managed by Niagara Parks (archived here) -- a body that describes itself as a "self-funded agency of the Government of Ontario under the Ministry of Tourism".
According to the official illumination calendar (archived here) on its website, the lights were not blue on Nov. 3, 2026, or around that day:

passages.title: Niagara Falls lit up blue after the Democrats’ victory in the United States
passages.passage:
Niagara Falls lit up blue after the Democrats’ victory in the United States
Photographs of Niagara Falls illuminated in blue appeared online after the U.S. congressional midterm elections, which were won by the Democratic Party. Social media users linked the unusual lighting to the voting results, UNN reports, citing the American radio station WBLK.
Radio journalists drew attention to photographs of Niagara Falls shared by users of the social network Threads. In the images, the falls are a deep blue, a color traditionally associated with the U.S. Democratic Party. Social media users suggested that Canada may have marked the Democrats’ success in the U.S. congressional midterm elections, held on November 3, in this way.
However, as WBLK notes, according to the official schedule, Niagara Falls was supposed to be illuminated not blue but turquoise that day. In particular, according to Niagara Parks, turquoise lighting was scheduled for November 3 from 10:00 p.m. to 10:15 p.m. local time to mark Alzheimer’s Disease Awareness Month. At the same time, the official calendar of special illuminations contains no mention of events dedicated to the U.S. elections.

Indian-American Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, who was backed by US President Donald Trump, has lost the Ohio governor's race to Democrat Amy Acton, the Press Trust of India reported.
Acton, 60, became the first woman elected governor of Ohio after securing more than 51 per cent of the votes. Ramaswamy, 41, received more than 45 per cent.
Days before the election, Ramaswamy faced criticism over an advertisement in which Acton's mother, Donna Arthur, called her daughter a liar and urged Ohio voters not to support her, PTI reported, citing NBC News.
Acton said she had neither seen nor spoken to Arthur in nearly 50 years. She has accused her mother's then-husband of sexually abusing her when she was a child, the report said.
Despite Trump's endorsement, support from prominent strategists and substantial campaign funding, Ramaswamy finished behind Acton, who secured a majority of the votes and became Ohio's first woman governor.

Despite their on-screen relationship being that of enemies, McKellen and Stewart have long been friends off-screen.
Hours after the news of Stewart's death broke, McKellen put out a lengthy post on Instagram, looking back on their friendship.
The actor further continued that Stewart “wore his heart on his sleeve.” As per McKellen, this attribute made him “a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love.”
McKellen recounted meeting with Stewart when they were both “ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago”. However, the two were not in the same productions at the time.

passages.passage:
Scott Colom, Mississippi’s Democratic U.S. Senate candidate, has flipped Forrest County, a once reliably Republican county named for the Ku Klux Klan's first Grand Wizard, Nathan Bedford Forrest.
With 97 percent of ballots counted, Colom led Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith 54 percent to 44 percent, reversing the 18-point advantage President Donald Trump secured in 2024 in Forrest County, which contains majority-Black Hattiesburg, home to the University of Southern Mississippi.
Forrest County’s 29-point movement toward Democrats is an important local boost for Colom, although the statewide Senate race remained too close to call on Friday morning as officials processed outstanding ballots.
Hyde-Smith’s campaign manager Jake Monssen said in a public statement: "We remain confident that when every legally cast vote is fully and accurately counted, Mississippians will have reelected Cindy Hyde-Smith." The campaign thanked election workers and said it was closely monitoring the remaining count.
The Forrest County result carries further historical weight as Colom seeks to become Mississippi’s first Black U.S. senator since Blanche K. Bruce left office in 1881.

The district attorney for Mississippi’s 16th Judicial District is hoping to become the state’s first Black Senator in nearly 150 years.
Colom would also be putting the Mississippi Democratic Party back into the Senate chambers.
But despite the historic stakes, Colom still has a fight ahead of him as votes continue to be counted across the Magnolia State.
As of Thursday morning, Colom holds a razor-thin lead of just 1,138 votes over Hyde-Smith, with 96% of the expected vote counted, according to the Associated Press.
“We remain confident that when every legally cast vote is fully and accurately counted, Mississippians will have reelected Cindy Hyde-Smith,” said campaign manager Jake Monssen.

JACKSON, Miss. (AP) — Scott Colom is a gregarious prosecutor who grew up in Mississippi with a Republican father who campaigned for Ronald Reagan and counted political titan Thad Cochran as a friend.
So, he’s an underdog in his bid to unseat Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, a white Donald Trump acolyte seeking her second full term. Yet several variables — Colom’s biography, Mississippi’s demographics, lingering inflation and Hyde-Smith’s understated profile — make for a wildcard matchup as Republicans defend their 53-47 Senate majority at the midpoint of Trump’s second presidency.

The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust also appointed three new members: Mahesh Bhagchandka, Madan Mohan Pandey and Nirmala Yadav. The appointments came against the backdrop of a controversy about the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Ram temple.
Jeetendra Mishra told The Hindu that he did not know about the appointment till the announcement was made on media outlets. “I also got to know about my selection through television,” he was quoted as saying by the newspaper. “I am elated for the same.”

passages.title: The Pentagon’s ‘FORTRESS’ initiative: what is it?
passages.passage:
Amid reports that the Pentagon is preparing U.S. military bases to remain operational for 90 days amid possible outside disruptions, much attention has suddenly fallen on the Department of War’s “FORTRESS America” initiative.
Although FORTRESS may just recently be in the spotlight this week, the initiative was unveiled in September, when Secretary of War Pete Hegseth described it as a “national insurance policy for the American homeland” during his “State of the Force” address in Quantico, Virginia.
The goal of this initiative is to ensure that U.S. military installations remain fully operational in the event of any type of attack or disruption.
“Every major military installation in America is going to generate its own power,” Hegseth said in September. “Independent of the civilian grid. If an adversary takes down the grid—by cyberattack, by sabotage, by any means—our bases stay lit. Our aircraft keep flying. Our command centers never go dark.”
In a memo sent to the DOW last month, Hegseth directed Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment Michael P. Duffey to organize and launch the initiative within 30 days, as of September 30.

passages.title: FORTRESS America: Will PNT Resilience Become a Pentagon Priority?
passages.passage:
On September 30, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced FORTRESS America, a new initiative intended to strengthen the nation’s ability to sustain military operations despite disruptions to critical infrastructure, supply chains and essential services.
For those concerned about America’s overdependence on GPS for positioning, navigation and timing (PNT), the initiative offers reason for optimism. More importantly, PNT resilience is explicitly identified as a priority in the Pentagon’s initial implementation guidance.
On October 6, Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment Michael Duffey issued a memorandum establishing the initial framework for FORTRESS America and designated Richard “Matt” O’Malley as interim director of the program office.
FORTRESS America places particular emphasis on ensuring that military installations can operate independently of vulnerable civilian power grids.
Will FORTRESS America accelerate these initiatives, establish more comprehensive requirements, or support an integrated architecture incorporating space-based, terrestrial and other complementary PNT technologies?
